question: When did the word of wisdom become mandatory?
text:
The Word of Wisdom became a **formal commitment for Latter-day Saints on September 9, 1851**, and a **temple recommend requirement under President Heber J. Grant in the early 1920s**. ([churchofjesuschrist.org](https://www.churchofjesuschrist.org/study/manual/doctrine-and-covenants-student-manual/section-89-the-word-of-wisdom?lang=eng&utm_source=openai))

- **February 27, 1833:** Joseph Smith received the revelation, now Doctrine and Covenants 89. It was originally given “not by commandment or constraint.” ([churchofjesuschrist.org](https://www.churchofjesuschrist.org/study/manual/doctrine-and-covenants-student-manual/section-89-the-word-of-wisdom?lang=eng&utm_source=openai))
- **September 9, 1851:** At general conference, members unanimously accepted Brigham Young’s proposal to covenant to keep it. In practice, expectations about strict observance still varied for decades. ([churchofjesuschrist.org](https://www.churchofjesuschrist.org/study/manual/doctrine-and-covenants-student-manual/section-89-the-word-of-wisdom?lang=eng&utm_source=openai))
- **1919–1921:** Official Church sources give different dates for the temple recommend requirement. The Church History Library dates it to **1919**, while the Church’s *Church History Topics* dates it to **1921**. ([churchhistorylibrary.churchofjesuschrist.org](https://churchhistorylibrary.churchofjesuschrist.org/blog/ask-us-top-reference-questions-about-the-word-of-wisdom?lang=eng&utm_source=openai))
